headline: Adams and Jefferson hang 190 on the league
card_headline: The best score of the season.
standfirst: Four weeks in, the league has a clear top three. Ben E., michael and CeeDeez Nutz are the three highest scorers, all averaging 138 or better, and a combined 106-26 when you line them up against every team every week. Behind them, the schedule is doing a lot of the talking. Team Galakrond has scored enough to be 2-2 and is 0-4 after facing 623 points, by far the most in the league. Bingo Night has scored like a half-win team and is 2-2. And Lyudmil just posted 190.06, the best single week anybody has had this season.
lede_scores: Closest game first. Ben E. stayed perfect by two tenths of a point. Gold border means it came down to less than ten.
lede_rankings: Record carries the most weight now, with recent form, scoring and luck behind it. Where a blurb mentions expected wins, that is a team's record against the whole league each week, scaled to four games: what its scoring has earned, regardless of schedule. The color bar splits this week's points by position.
lede_positions: This week's points by position. Look at Team Galakrond's backfield, then at the rest of that row. Ben E. and CeeDeez Nutz have the best receiver rooms in the league over four weeks, each about 22 points a week above average.

labels.lede_season: Four weeks on the board. Bingo Night drops five spots, the biggest fall of the season. Adams and Jefferson climbs three.
labels.cnote: Rank one at the top. Every Monday night adds a column.

takes.2: The only unbeaten team, and the record holds up. Ben E. is 37-7 against the whole league over four weeks, scoring between 131 and 151 every week. The engine is the receiver room, about 22 points a week above league average, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba at 116.7 on the season. The backfield is the thin spot, about four a week below average. Expected wins are 3.36, so there is a little luck in the 4-0, most visibly this week's 0.2 point escape against CeeDeez Nutz. Still a legitimate first-place team.
takes.9: michael leads the league in total points at 574.6 and is 36-8 against the field. Jahmyr Gibbs (116.0 on the season) and Josh Allen (112.5) are the best quarterback and backfield pairing in the league, about 10 a week above average at QB and 19 at RB. Receivers are average and the tight end spot is below it. The real story is the bench: 319.2 points left there across four weeks, about 80 a week and the most in the league by a distance. This week's 125.9 was his season low, and he still won.
takes.3: The most consistent team in the league: 138.7, 147.3, 133.6, 133.2. CeeDee Lamb went for 41.3, the second-best individual score of the week, and the receiver room runs about 22 a week above average, level with Ben E.'s for best in the league. The backfield is the weakness, about 14 a week below average. The one loss came by 0.2 with 88.7 points on the bench. Expected wins of 3.00 match the record exactly. This team is right where it should be.
takes.8: The most volatile team in the league: 177.9, 56.5, 96.5, 131.4. Javonte Williams (81.8 on the season) and Ashton Jeanty (73.9) make the backfield about 12 a week above average. Receivers run about 15 below, though Puka Nacua's 27.7 this week helps. Dake has also had the gentlest schedule, facing the fewest points in the league at 386.1, which is how a team that is 23-21 against the field gets to 3-1. The 462.2 total points rank seventh.
takes.7: A mid-pack team with a clear shape. Bijan Robinson (105.4 on the season) and Brock Purdy (100.5) carry the scoring, and Trey McBride has the tight end spot about seven a week above average. The receivers are the problem, about 15 a week below average, and this week they produced two zeros: Rashee Rice and Jalen Coker. Expected wins of 2.18 match the 2-2 record. Fix the receiver room and this is a top-four team.
takes.5: 190.06. The best single-week score in the league this season, 12.2 clear of Dake's week-one 177.86. Tetairoa McMillan's 45.2 was the top individual score of the week, Kyren Williams added 36.7, and the receivers and backfield combined for 128.6. Lyudmil is fourth in total points at 521.0 and exactly 22-22 against the field, which usually means two wins, not one. The difference is the schedule: 544.3 points faced, second-most in the league. Quarterback is still unsettled, three different starters in four weeks, with Bryce Young's 21.5 this week the best of them. Justin Jefferson was not in the lineup. The power score has noticed all of it and moves this team up three spots.
takes.4: Up five spots last week, back down two this week. Derrick Henry (90.8 on the season) and Dak Prescott (81.2) carry the scoring, and the team sits right around league average at quarterback and running back. Receivers run about six a week below average, and Ja'Marr Chase has been streaky: 3.2, 26.5, 24.8, 5.7. At 15-29 against the field, expected wins are 1.36, so 2-2 is running slightly ahead of the scoring. Another 276.3 points have been left on the bench, second-most in the league.
takes.11: The league's most predictable middle team, landing between 94.8 and 114.9 every week. Drake Maye's 26.2 was the best quarterback score in the league this week, after 9.8, 8.0 and 3.8 to start the year. Amon-Ra St. Brown (91.3 on the season) and Sam LaPorta keep receiver and tight end above average. The backfield runs about 10 a week below. Expected wins of 1.55 say 2-2 is a little ahead of the scoring.
takes.12: Steady, between 102 and 124 every week, and very unlucky in close ones: a 0.4 point loss in week two and a 2.5 point loss this week. kelly has also faced 511.1 points, fourth-most in the league. Joe Burrow, Christian McCaffrey and Tee Higgins have each scored between 71 and 77 on the season, which is depth without a true star. The defense has finished at zero in three of four weeks.
takes.10: Finally on the board. This week's 118.1 was a season high, built on Nico Collins (30.8) and Malik Nabers (23.2). The season numbers are still rough: at or below average at every position, and 11-33 against the field, second-worst in the league. Expected wins of 1.00 match the record. This week's receiver output is the template, if it can be repeated.
takes.1: The unluckiest team in the league, and it is not close. Neil has faced 623.1 points, 78.8 more than anyone else. The 22-22 record against the field says two wins, and the standings say zero. Kenneth Walker (110.1 on the season) and Jonathan Taylor (86.2) make this the best backfield in the league, about 26 a week above average. The receivers are the league's worst, about 18 a week below, and quarterback is the lowest in the league too. This week he scored 140.28, second-best in the league, and ran into the season high.
takes.6: The other side of the luck ledger. At 6-38 against the field, Bingo Night's scoring is worth about half a win, and the record shows two. Fewest points in the league at 368.7, and the lowest score of the week two weeks running. The backfield is the biggest hole, about 18 a week below average, with Saquon Barkley at 9.0, 3.0, 9.0 and 2.0. The record is fine for now. The power rankings have stopped giving credit for it.

og_description: The best score of the season, a clear top three, and the schedule deciding more games than anyone would like.
